cluster_summary: Judged from code, the open ground in this cluster is company-level linkage of India's industrial filings: iem-tracker (IEM Part A to Part B to CIN, checked against GLEIF) has no free equivalent, and the PIB/CCI/SEBI SQLite indexes in india-trade-sector-policy-recommendations plus the PARIVESH bulk-endpoint pivot in india-ec-subsector-analysis are useful new tooling. The five trade repos overlap heavily: india-trade-tracker is the only tested collector (HS-2 TradeStat + World Bank); india-trade-data-analysis and india-commodity-trade-deficit are JSON/HTML narratives with no generating code and share the same 98-chapter TradeStat file; india-trade-export-analysis holds one-off pandas scripts whose write-ups were copied, reformatted, into india-forex-analysis, which has no code. The biggest README-vs-code gap is in those last two: headline totals ($875B exports, -$567B deficit, -$769.5B projection) are about 2x official TradeStat figures, consistent with the scripts summing every xlsx row including the total row, and the reserve-cover, debt and budget figures have no generating script. digital-twin-for-ipa does not simulate PLI schemes: it tabulates hand-verified scheme records and counts sectors per state, so the 'incentive simulation against a company database' gap the August survey credited to it is still open. india-ec-subsector-analysis's grant rate drops rejected proposals from the denominator, which inflates every activity's rate. No repo implements RCA, Grubel-Lloyd or import penetration, though several are framed around those questions.

tot_f, tot_i = sum(fdi.values()), sum(iem.values())
    states = sorted(set(fdi) | set(iem))
    rows = []
    for st in states:
        f, i = fdi.get(st), iem.get(st)
        fs = (f / tot_f * 100) if (f is not None and tot_f) else None
        isf = (i / tot_i * 100) if (i is not None and tot_i) else None
        # NB: test for None, not truthiness -- a state with a genuinely tiny share
        # (Assam: 0.004% of FDI) rounds to 0.00 and would be silently dropped.
        ratio = (fs / isf) if (fs is not None and isf) else None
        rows.append({
            "state": st,
            "fdi_usd_mn": round(f, 2) if f is not None else None,
            "fdi_share_pct": round(fs, 2) if fs is not None else None,
            "iem_implemented_rs_cr": round(i, 2) if i is not None else None,
            "iem_share_pct": round(isf, 2) if isf is not None else None,
            "intensity_ratio": round(ratio, 4) if ratio is not None else None,
snippets.why: The one quantitative indicator coded here: a state's FDI share divided by its share of implemented IEM investment - a location-quotient-style ratio, not RCA/TII.

                print(f"WARNING: {state}: repeated empty pages at "

            time.sleep(60)

def log_event(db, step: str, input_text: str, output_text: str,
              model: str = "", prompt_ver: str = "") -> str:
    """Append a provenance event chained to the previous one's hash."""
    row = db.execute("SELECT hash FROM prov_event ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 1").fetchone()
    prev = row[0] if row else ""
    ts = time.time()
    body = json.dumps([prev, step, model, prompt_ver, sha(input_text), sha(output_text), ts])
    h = sha(body)
    db.execute("INSERT INTO prov_event(prev_hash,step,model,prompt_ver,input_sha,output_sha,ts,hash)"
               " VALUES(?,?,?,?,?,?,?,?)",
               (prev, step, model, prompt_ver, sha(input_text), sha(output_text), ts, h))
    db.commit()
    return h
snippets.why: Tamper-evident provenance: each LLM event hashes the previous event's hash with input/output digests, so verify_chain can detect edits.

def _declares_dark(body):
    """Whether the post actually declares a dark palette -- ignoring the
    strings inside HTML/CSS comments, so a comment that only *discusses*
    prefers-color-scheme (e.g. to explain why it was deliberately left out)
    doesn't trip a false BLOCKER. Caught on quarterly-reportage-4034-scheme,
    whose own explanatory comment contains the literal phrase."""
    stripped = _COMMENT_RE.sub("", body)
    return ("prefers-color-scheme" in stripped) or ('data-theme="dark"' in stripped)
snippets.why: Typical house-style rule: strip comments before deciding whether a post declares a dark palette, a rule born from a real false positive.
